maya: Heads up — I pushed a tiny sample app to the next-playground repo that wires Redwood SDK -> LangChain adapter. When running locally behind our dev proxy (next dev), the SDK sometimes throws a 401 or immediately retries twice and fails. No errors in the console beyond the 401. Anyone seen auth+retry weirdness on Edge/experimental runtimes?

owen: Hmm, saw something like that last week but thought it was my env. What error string do you get?

maya: Logs:```
Error: 401 Unauthorized
 at fetch (node:internal/process/next_tick:...)
 at RedwoodClient.request (/workspace/packages/sdk/src/index.ts:324)
 Caused by: fetch failed with status 401
```
Config I'm using (simplified):```js
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_BASE || 'https://api.redwood.example',
  retry: { retries: 3, backoff: 300 }
})
```
I tested both cookie auth on the dev proxy and a bearer header. Bearer header still 401s occasionally and then the SDK retries immediately (so my app hits rate limits on the proxy).

dev-bot: Deployed sample-next-playground @maya -> main (sha: c4f9e2d) :rocket:

jen: A couple guesses: 1) Next dev server sometimes proxies requests with altered headers (esp. when using custom rewrites). 2) The Edge runtime (middleware/route handlers) requires you to use fetch-based auth injection — you can't mutate Request.headers same way in edge.

jen: Try changing the auth path to explicitly set Authorization on an outgoing fetch:```js
// edge-compatible helper
export function withAuth(req) {
  const headers = new Headers(req.headers);
  headers.set('authorization', `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`);
  return new Request(req.url, { method: req.method, headers, body: req.body });
}
```
Also make sure you have next.config.experimental.runtime: 'edge' only where you intend it.

sam: Another gotcha: the SDK's default retry backoff is naive for local proxies. It retries immediately when it sees network errors, which can amplify auth races. We added an env var REDWOOD_RETRY_JITTER in our infra to avoid thundering herd. For the sample app, maybe include a small retry wrapper that uses exponential backoff + jitter.

owen: +1 to including a tiny helper in the repo. Something like:
```js
async function retryable(fn, attempts = 3){
  for(let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try { return await fn(); }
    catch(e){ if(i===attempts-1) throw e; await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, Math.pow(2,i)*200 + Math.random()*100)); }
  }
}
```

maya: Thanks — I just pushed a quick patch that changes the sample to use withAuth + the retryable helper and added a README note about "Edge runtime auth quirks" and the dev proxy. It seems stable in my local testing now.
